source_text: Πατρὸς, νῦν ἐμφανισθῆναι λέγεται ὡς ἐν ἑαυτῷ γε καὶ πρώτῳ παρατιθεὶς ἐν ὄψει τοῦ Πατρὸς τὰ ἀνθρώπινα, καὶ τὴν ἀρχαίαν ἐκείνην ἀποστροφὴν μεθιστάς. «Αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστιν ἡ εἰρήνη ἡμῶν,» κατὰ τὰς Γραφάς. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἄραρεν οὖν ὅτι Χριστοῦ πάλιν εἰκὼν τὸ θυσιαστήριον τὸ χρυσοῦν. {ΚΥΡ.} Καὶ πρός γε δὴ τούτῳ νοοῖτ' ἂν εἰκότως αὐτὸς ὁ θυμίαμα τὸ σύνθετον καὶ λεπτόν. Αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ ἀρχιερεύς· «Θυμιάσει γὰρ,» φησὶν, «ἐπ' αὐτοῦ Ἀαρὼν θυμίαμα σύνθετον, λεπτόν·» καὶ σύνθετον μὲν τὸ θυμίαμα· Θεὸς γὰρ ὢν ὁ Λόγος, γέγονε σάρξ. Καὶ συντέθειταί πως ἡμῖν ὁ Ἐμμανουὴλ, θείας φύσεώς τε καὶ ἀνθρωπότητος εἰς ἐνότητα τὴν ὑπὲρ νοῦν, ἀποῤῥήτως συνηνεγμένην. Λεπτὸν δὲ, ὅτι τὸ παχὺ τῆς κατὰ νόμον λατρείας οὐκ ἔχει. «Θυσίας γὰρ καὶ προσφορὰν οὐκ ἠθέλησας. Ὁλοκαύτωμα καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας οὐκ εὐδόκησας. Σῶμα δὲ κατηρτίσω μοι, φησί· τότε εἶπον, Ἰδοὺ ἥκω· τοῦ ποιῆσαι, ὁ Θεὸς, τὸ θέλημά σου.» Καὶ τί δὴ τοῦτό ἐστι τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Πατρὸς, αὐτὸς ἡμᾶς ἐν Εὐαγγελίοις μεμυσταγώγηκε λέγων, ὅτι «Καταβέβηκα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, οὐχ ἵνα ποιῶ τὸ θέλημα τὸ ἐμὸν, ἀλλὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με. Τοῦτο δέ ἐστι τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πεμψαντός με, ἵνα πᾶν ὃ δέδωκέ μοι, μὴ ἀπολέσω ἐξ αὐτοῦ, ἀλλὰ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸ ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.» Προσκεκόμικε γὰρ ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας, κεχρημάτικέ τε διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἀρχιερεύς. Οὐκοῦν αὐτὸς ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς, αὐτὸς τὸ θυμίαμα τὸ σύνθετόν τε καὶ λεπτόν· καὶ μαρτυρήσει λέγων ὁ Παῦλος· «Τῷ δὲ Θεῷ χάρις, τῷ πάντοτε θριαμβεύοντι ἡμᾶς ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ, καὶ τὴν ὀσμὴν τῆς γνώσεως αὐτοῦ φανεροῦντι δι' ἡμῶν ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ, ὅτι Χριστοῦ εὐωδία ἐσμὲν τῷ Θεῷ, ἐν τοῖς σωζομένοις, καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις· οἷς μὲν ὀσμὴ ἐκ θανάτου εἰς θάνατον, οἷς δὲ ὀσμὴ ζωῆς εἰς ζωήν.» Προσεφώνει δὲ καὶ ἡμῖν· «Γίνεσθε οὖν μιμηταὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ ὡς τέκνα ἀγαπητὰ, καὶ περιπατεῖτε ἐν ἀγάπῃ, καθὼς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς ἠγάπησεν ἡμᾶς, καὶ παρέδωκεν ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν προσφορὰν καὶ θυσίαν τῷ Θεῷ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας.» Καὶ τόν γε τοῦ θυμιᾷν ἐναργῆ καθίστη καιρὸν, ἅπαντα δὲ δεῖν ἐν τάξει τε καὶ εὐκοσμίᾳ πράττεσθαι νομοθετῶν, καὶ δι' ὧν ἂν ἡμῖν ἡ τῶν εἰς τὸ εἴσω θεωρημάτων εὖ ἔχοι δύναμις. «Τὸ πρωῒ» γὰρ, φησὶ, «καὶ τὸ ὀψὲ τῶν λύχνων ἐξαπτομένων καὶ ἐπισκιαζομένων,» τοῦ μὲν ὀψὲ καὶ πρωῒ, τὸ ἀδιάλειπτόν τε καὶ διηνεκὲς ἐμφαίνοντος, τοῦ δὲ ὑπὸ λύχνοις χρῆναι θυμιᾷν, ἐκεῖνό που τάχα παραδηλοῦντος εὖ μάλα, ὅτι φωτὶ τῷ θείῳ καταλαμπόμενοι, τότε δὴ, τότε τῆς εὐωδίας Χριστοῦ πλουσίως ἀναπιμπλάμεθα, ἴμεν τε οὕτω πρὸς αἴσθησιν τῶν ἔσω σκηνῆς ἀγαθῶν, ἤτοι τῆς τῶν θείων χαρισμάτων διανομῆς, ἣν τοῖς ἀξίοις ὀρέγει Χριστός· Ὥστε εἴ τις οὔπω γέγονεν ἐν φωτὶ διὰ πίστεως, ἔστι που πάντως καὶ τῆς νοητῆς εὐωδίας ἀμέτοχος, ἔτι τὸ Χριστοῦ μὴ εἰδὼς μυστήριον.
pass_a_gloss: CYR. (cont.) …Father, is said 'now to be manifested' (ἐμφανισθῆναι), as in himself and first setting beside (παρατιθείς) in the sight (ὄψις) of the Father the human things (τὰ ἀνθρώπινα), and removing (μεθιστάς) that ancient turning-away (ἀποστροφή). 'For he is our peace (εἰρήνη),' according to the Scriptures. PALL.: It has fitted (ἄραρεν), then, that the golden altar is again an image (εἰκών) of Christ. CYR.: And in addition to this he himself would fittingly be understood as the incense compound (σύνθετον) and fine (λεπτόν). For he himself is the high priest (ἀρχιερεύς): 'For Aaron will burn on it compound, fine incense'; compound the incense, for the Word being God became flesh (σάρξ). And Emmanuel has in a way been compounded (συντέθειται) for us, divine nature (φύσις θεία) and humanity (ἀνθρωπότης) into the unity (ἑνότης) beyond mind (ὑπὲρ νοῦν), ineffably (ἀπορρήτως) brought together (συνηνεγμένην). Fine, because it does not have the thick/coarse (τὸ παχύ) of the worship (λατρεία) according to law. 'Sacrifices (θυσίαι) and offering (προσφορά) you did not will; burnt-offering (ὁλοκαύτωμα) and [offering] for sin you were not pleased with; but a body (σῶμα) you prepared (κατηρτίσω) for me, he says; then I said, Behold, I come to do, O God, your will (θέλημα).' And what this will of the Father is, he himself initiated us into (μεμυσταγώγηκε) in the Gospels, saying: 'I have come down from heaven not to do my will but the will of the one who sent me. This is the will of the one who sent me, that all which he has given me I should not lose of it, but raise (ἀναστήσω) it on the last day.' For he brought (προσκεκόμικε) himself for us into an odour of sweet fragrance (ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας), and therefore has been styled (κεχρημάτικε) high priest. Therefore he himself the high priest, he himself the incense compound and fine; and Paul will bear witness saying: 'Thanks to God who always leads us in triumph (θριαμβεύοντι) in Christ, and manifests (φανεροῦντι) the odour of the knowledge (γνῶσις) of him through us in every place; for we are a fragrance (εὐωδία) of Christ to God in those being saved and in those perishing; to these an odour from death to death, to those an odour of life to life.' And he called to us: 'Become imitators (μιμηταί) of God as beloved children, and walk in love (ἀγάπη), as Christ loved us and handed over (παρέδωκεν) himself for us an offering and sacrifice to God into an odour of sweet fragrance.' And he set (καθίστη) a clear (ἐναργῆ) time (καιρός) for burning incense, legislating (νομοθετῶν) that all things must be done in order (τάξις) and good order (εὐκοσμία), and through the things by which the force (δύναμις) of the contemplations (θεωρήματα) toward the inside (εἰς τὸ εἴσω) would be well for us. 'In the morning,' he says, 'and in the evening, the lamps being kindled and shaded (ἐπισκιαζομένων)': the evening and morning showing the unceasing (ἀδιάλειπτον) and perpetual (διηνεκές); the needing to burn incense under lamps perhaps indicating (παραδηλοῦντος) very well that being illumined (καταλαμπόμενοι) by the divine light (φῶς), then indeed, then we are richly filled (ἀναπιμπλάμεθα) with the fragrance of Christ, and so we go (ἴμεν) to perception (αἴσθησις) of the goods inside the tent, that is, the distribution (διανομή) of the divine gifts (χαρίσματα), which Christ holds out (ὀρέγει) to the worthy (ἄξιοι). So if anyone has not yet come to be in light through faith (πίστις), he is surely without share (ἀμέτοχος) also in the intelligible fragrance (νοητὴ εὐωδία), not yet knowing the mystery (μυστήριον) of Christ.
pass_b_english: Cyril: …Father, is said ‘now to appear,’ because in himself, as the first, he sets human nature in the Father’s sight and removes that ancient turning away. ‘For he is our peace’ (Ephesians 2:14), as the Scriptures say.
Palladius: So it is settled that the golden altar is again an image of Christ.

Cyril: And besides this, he himself may fittingly be understood as the compound and fine incense. For he himself is the high priest: ‘For Aaron,’ he says, ‘shall burn on it compound, fine incense’ (Exodus 30:7). The incense is compound, for the Word, being God, became flesh (John 1:14). Emmanuel is in a way compounded for us, divine nature and humanity being brought together, beyond words, into a unity beyond understanding. And it is fine, because it has nothing of the coarseness of worship under the law. ‘For sacrifices and offering you did not desire; in burnt offering and sin offering you took no pleasure. But a body you prepared for me,’ he says; ‘then I said, Behold, I have come to do your will, O God’ (Hebrews 10:5–7; Psalm 40:6–8). And what this will of the Father is, he himself has taught us in the Gospels, saying: ‘I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me. And this is the will of him who sent me, that of all that he has given me I should lose nothing, but raise it up on the last day’ (John 6:38–39). For he offered himself for us as a fragrant aroma, and for this reason he was also named high priest. So he himself is the high priest, and he himself is the compound and fine incense. Paul will bear witness, saying: ‘But thanks be to God, who always leads us in triumph in Christ, and through us reveals the fragrance of the knowledge of him in every place. For we are the aroma of Christ to God among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing: to some a fragrance from death to death, to others a fragrance of life to life’ (2 Corinthians 2:14–16). And he called to us as well: ‘Be imitators of God, therefore, as beloved children, and walk in love, just as Christ also loved us and gave himself up for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God as a fragrant aroma’ (Ephesians 5:1–2). He also fixed a clear time for burning incense, laying down that everything must be done in order and with propriety, and by means that would make plain to us the force of the insights that point inward. ‘In the morning,’ he says, ‘and in the evening, when the lamps are lit and shaded’ (Exodus 30:7–8). The evening and the morning show what is unceasing and continual. The need to burn incense by lamplight perhaps hints very well at this: when we are lit by the divine light, it is then, truly then, that we are richly filled with the fragrance of Christ, and so we come to perceive the good things within the tent, that is, the distribution of the divine gifts of grace that Christ holds out to the worthy. So if anyone has not yet come into the light through faith, he surely has no share in the spiritual fragrance either, since he does not yet know the mystery of Christ.

choices.why: 'τὰ ἀνθρώπινα' (the human things) rendered 'human nature'; could also be 'human affairs'.
'νοητὴ εὐωδία' rendered 'spiritual fragrance' (fragrance perceived by the mind).
'ὑπὸ λύχνοις' read as 'by lamplight' (while the lamps burn).

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opening sentence completes section 17 ('he who always exists with his own Father is said "now to appear"'), picking up Hebrews 9:24, which is cited in section 17; not re-cited here. 'For he is our peace' = Ephesians 2:14 (the old English cited Ephesians 5:1–2 here, which was wrong). 'τὰ ἀνθρώπινα' (the human things) rendered 'human nature'; could also be 'human affairs'. The Psalm quotation follows the Hebrews 10:5–7 form ('a body you prepared', with 'θυσίας καὶ προσφοράν'), with the clauses in Cyril's own order (burnt offering line before 'a body'); Hebrew/English Psalm 40:6–8 = LXX Psalm 39:7–9; the Hebrew has 'ears you have dug' for 'a body'. 'Θυσίας' may be accusative plural or genitive; rendered as the Hebrews singular sense 'sacrifice'. 'Fragrant aroma' (εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας) in 'he offered himself for us' anticipates Ephesians 5:2, quoted in full below; not cited separately. 'κεχρημάτικε... ἀρχιερεύς' (was styled high priest) may echo Hebrews 5:10; uncited as doubtful. 'ἐν τάξει τε καὶ εὐκοσμίᾳ' is near 1 Corinthians 14:40 in sense but not in wording; uncited. 'Lit and shaded': Cyril's text of Exodus 30:7–8 has ἐπισκιάζω (see note at section 16; LXX standard ἐπισκευάζω, 'trims'). 'νοητὴ εὐωδία' rendered 'spiritual fragrance' (fragrance perceived by the mind). 'ἴμεν' read as 1st plural of εἶμι ('we go/come'). Reviewer: Cyril's text of 2 Corinthians 2:16 reads 'ὀσμὴ ζωῆς εἰς ζωήν' (no ἐκ), so 'of life to life'. 'ὑπὸ λύχνοις' read as 'by lamplight' (while the lamps burn).

changes: 2 Corinthians 2:16: 'from life to life' -> 'of life to life' (Cyril's text has no ἐκ); οἷς μὲν/οἷς δὲ -> 'to some/to others'
'seemliness' (archaic) and stiff 'inner meanings would reach us well' clause rewritten
'then, and only then' -> 'then, truly then' (τότε δή, τότε; 'only' was an addition)

reviewer: Claude (fresh translation from the Greek + independent clause review), 2026-10-23
